text: Final categorization: OK (Justification: This is a non-review research paper focused centrally on spatially explicit land-use change prediction for the contiguous United States (national scale). The study uses an econometric land-use model to project future land-use change from 2001 to 2051 under two distinct baseline scenarios and three policy scenarios, thus implementing multiple future scenarios with quantitative comparisons. The model produces mapped LULC projections at 100-m resolution, and the predictions include quantitative assessments of land cover changes, ecosystem service impacts, and species habitat changes. The paper explicitly discusses spatial modeling with county-soil-level transition matrices and land-use maps, thus demonstrating spatial explicitness. The analysis includes quantitative metrics of change rates and land cover transitions. Hence, it meets all core inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria. The primary objective is LULC prediction and simulation, not incidental use.)
